tex_content.html:
Proposition

↗ prop:existence-riemannian-metric ↗ prop:riemannian-distance-finite ↗ def:riemannian-distance

1. ch2:2.50Any two points of a connected smooth manifold, with or without boundary, can be joined by an admissible curve.
Proof

↗ prop:existence-riemannian-metric ↗ prop:riemannian-distance-finite ↗ def:riemannian-distance \sketch A continuous path exists by connectedness and path connectedness. Compactness permits a partition whose image segments lie in coordinate balls or boundary half-balls; replace each by a coordinate line segment. Alternatively, choose a metric by Proposition 2; Proposition 15 and the distance definition provide a finite-length competitor.

□

On a disconnected Riemannian manifold, $d_g(p,q)$ is also used when $p$ and $q$ belong to the same connected component.
